strengths: The global workspace layer offers a worthwhile architectural combination of low-dimensional shared memory, sparse token selection, and associative retrieval. Its integration into a conventional vision Transformer is straightforward.

The reported results support improved parameter efficiency relative to the tested ViT baselines. AiT-Medium uses 45.9M parameters versus ViT-Base's 85.7M, while improving CIFAR-100 accuracy from 57.92% to 60.58% and ImageNet100 accuracy from 34.62% to 36.72% (Tables 1–2).

The relational reasoning improvements are substantial within the evaluated setting: AiT-Base achieves 80.03% on Sort-of-CLEVR relational questions, compared with 73.43% for Coordination and 63.35% for ViT-Base (Table 6).

The component ablations provide useful empirical evidence. Removing the bottleneck reduces CIFAR-10 accuracy from 83.34% to 75.40%, while removing the balance loss reduces it to 81.89% (Table 3). Repeated experiments with reported variability, the compact-model comparison in Figure 3, and supplementary attention visualizations strengthen the evaluation.
weaknesses: The selected-instance component of the proposed balance loss is not a trainable balancing signal as specified. In Equation 3, A is defined using dense softmax, so every entry is positive, every load equals M, and the load-variance term is zero. If A instead means the attention after top-k masking, the hard positivity indicator has zero derivative almost everywhere; no differentiable estimator is described. The combined-loss ablation does not establish that this claimed component contributes. This is a substantive issue in a central methodological claim.

The Hopfield interpretation overstates what the implemented retrieval establishes. For the stated energy, the standard single-step update is dot-product attention with identical memory keys and values. Consequently, the comparison against a larger, projected multi-head cross-attention module does not isolate a distinct benefit from energy minimization. Furthermore, one update does not generally compute the argmin written in Equation 6 or guarantee that all tokens reach their minima simultaneously. Figure 9 supports energy reduction, which is weaker than these convergence claims. The contribution is therefore better supported as an architectural integration than as a new retrieval mechanism.

The memory state during evaluation is insufficiently specified. Section 3.2 says explicit memory is frozen during evaluation, but Appendix F evaluates the contribution of the memory-writing cross-attention at test time. The manuscript does not clearly distinguish fixed stored priors, temporary input-conditioned updates, and persistent EMA updates, or specify resetting and gradient handling across batches. Because tokens are pooled across examples, these distinctions affect batch dependence and reproducibility of the reported results.

The broad superiority claims exceed the comparative evidence. Table 6 omits the relation-network model introduced in reference [14], although it includes that work's CNN+LSTM baseline, and does not evaluate the more recent relational architectures cited in the introduction. Main-model comparisons against Coordination also involve substantially different parameter and computation budgets. Figure 3 provides a useful compact-block control, but cannot establish the same efficiency advantage for the complete models across tasks.

The efficiency evidence primarily establishes benefits from reducing depth. Figure 1 retains dense self-attention, and the bottleneck computes dense memory-to-token scores before selecting top-k entries. Parameter counts and FLOPs are informative, but runtime, peak memory, and sequence-length scaling are not evaluated, leaving the practical computational advantage of the sparse mechanism unresolved.

Additional reporting issues hinder reproduction: Section 4.1 specifies an initial learning rate of 1e-5, whereas Table 8 lists 1e-4; ImageNet100 class selection and the validation protocol for hyperparameter search are unspecified. These are more readily correctable than the core loss and memory-procedure concerns, but the promised future code release cannot resolve them in the submitted manuscript.
